title: I Posted the Reuse-Store Test-Bench Photo After They Sold My Hold Untested

parts.text: I tagged a receiver HOLD 24H at 11:14 a.m. after the test bench failed power. At 11:41 it was on the sold rack with a TESTED sticker. The bench card said: FAIL STAYS. HOLD 24H. NO STICKER ON FAIL. Clerk Ron shrugged. "Holds are vibes." I was thirty-eight, buyer, holding the fail printout. I photographed the fail, the sticker, and the rack. Then I logged a sell. At 11:48 the reuse manager asked why Ron's sticker was on a fail hold. I let them finish the sentence they would regret in writing. Petty is a word people use when their name is on the ticket.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The reuse manager can see a TESTED sticker on a receiver that failed the bench.

social.video_title: They sold my failed hold with a tested sticker — Part 1/2
social.description: Reuse store, a 24h hold, and a fail printout. I logged the sell. Would you have photographed the sticker?

parts.text: Ron called it a retest until the manager asked for the log. I printed the sell, the photo, and the card. The receiver came off the rack. Ron retested on camera and told the floor retests were always about optics. Optics is a word stickers use when a fail exists. Test policy now has a second line: FAILS STAY. I keep the printout. Ron benches. The store finally looks like a bench, not a vibe. Nobody thanked me, which is how you know a policy finally works. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.

social.description: Sell log, receiver off the rack, and a second line. Was a retest ever a sticker?
